TableChat.title: Components/TableChat
TableChat.description:
# Table Chat Feature

The Table Chat feature provides a comprehensive real-time messaging system integrated with TableV36. It includes:

- **Channel Management**: Organize conversations by channels
- **Real-time Messaging**: Live message updates with WebSocket support
- **Rich Text Editor**: Full-featured text editor with mentions, formatting, and emoji support
- **File & Image Sharing**: Upload and share files and images
- **Message Actions**: Pin, reply, bookmark, edit, and delete messages
- **Participant Management**: Add/remove participants and manage permissions
- **Search**: Search messages and participants
- **Notifications**: Configurable notification settings
- **Thread Support**: Threaded conversations for better organization

## Architecture

The chat feature consists of several key components:

### 1. TableChatSidePanel
The main container component that manages the chat interface state and handles the communication between left and right panels.

### 2. TableChatRightSection
Handles the message display, infinite scroll, real-time updates, and message interactions.

### 3. ChatInput
Rich text editor with mention support, formatting tools, file upload, and emoji picker.

### 4. ChatHeader
Header with participant management, search functionality, and notification settings.

## Configuration Structure

The chat feature is configured through a comprehensive \

isChatEnabled.description: Enables the chat feature in the table component

handleChatClick.description: Handler function called when chat button is clicked

isChatOpen.description: Controls whether the chat panel is open

handleChatClose.description: Handler function called when chat panel is closed

chatConfiguration.description: Comprehensive chat configuration object (messageChatConfig, headerChatConfig, inputChatConfig, leftPanel, rightPanel)

Alert.title: Components/Alert
Alert.description:
An alert is a UI component used to notify users of important information, warnings, or errors. Alerts typically appear as banners or pop-ups and often require user acknowledgment.

General Guidelines for Writing Descriptions for Alerts
  • Brevity: Keep the message short and to the point.
  • Clarity: Clearly communicate the purpose of the alert and any required actions.
  • Tone: Match the tone to the severity of the message (informational, warning, error, etc.).
  • Actionable: If an action is needed, clearly state what the user should do next.

onClose.description: Event handler for close button (if missing, will not show close button)

Badge.title: Components/Badge
Badge.description:
A badge is a small UI component that often appears as a label or icon, usually attached to another element like an avatar, button, or notification. Badges can convey various types of information, such as status, counts, or categories.

General Guidelines for Writing Descriptions for Badges

  • Purpose: Clearly state the purpose of the badge (e.g., notification count, status indicator).
  • Clarity: Ensure the message is straightforward and unambiguous.
  • Relevance: Include relevant details, such as numbers or labels, and explain their significance.

If true, customWeekNumberData decides which fiscal week and fiscal month each date belongs to. Dates are shown in the calendar panel matching their fiscal_year_month (grid layout unchanged). Week labels (with showWeekNumbers) and the Week / Month / Quarter / Year range selector follow the fiscal data. Each record has the format,
  • calendar_week_start_date: UTC-midnight timestamp (ms) [number]
  • fiscal_year_week: e.g. 202541 [number]
  • fiscal_year_month: e.g. 202510 [number]

 Falls back to the default behavior when the data is missing or empty.
